nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light drives the algae of the clear lake, the reed beds and the crops and vines of the shore.

nodes.name: Karst springs and Prespa seepage
nodes.desc: Springs on the eastern shore give about half of the lake's inflow, and over a fifth comes underground from Lake Prespa.

nodes.name: Clear, low-nutrient water
nodes.desc: Ohrid is oligotrophic, with very low phosphorus and clarity to about 22 m, which suits its many endemic species.

nodes.name: Phosphorus inputs
nodes.desc: Household wastewater has raised phosphorus in the sediments about 3.5-fold in a century, a main threat to the lake.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead algae, reeds, fish and land animals, returning nutrients to the water and soil.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton and algae
nodes.desc: Drifting microscopic algae, including about 20 endemic algae species in Ohrid, feed the zooplankton and snails.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Forms reed beds along wetland shores. Most Ohrid shore wetlands have been drained, and the reed belt is under pressure from building.

nodes.name: Grape vine
nodes.desc: Wild and grown vines on the sunny shores. GloBI records link its fruit to foxes, bears, martens and dormice.

nodes.name: Maize
nodes.desc: A farm crop around the lake. GloBI records show wood mice and brown bears eating it.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans of open water. Ohrid has about five endemic zooplankton species. General ecology: they graze algae.

nodes.name: Endemic lake snails
nodes.desc: About 73 percent of freshwater snails in the basin are endemic. General ecology: many graze algae on the lake bed.

nodes.name: Albanian roach
nodes.desc: A small fish of large, nutrient-poor lakes in the Ohrid and Skadar drainages. One of eight endemic cyprinids in Ohrid.

nodes.name: Edible dormouse
nodes.desc: Forest and orchard rodent recorded near the lake. GloBI links it to grapes and dwarf elder.

nodes.name: Wood mouse
nodes.desc: A common small rodent of the shore scrub and fields that eats crop seed such as maize and is prey for many predators.

nodes.name: Ohrid trout
nodes.desc: An endemic, endangered trout that preys on smaller fish. Overfishing and illegal fishing have cut its numbers.

nodes.name: European eel
nodes.desc: Eats fish and molluscs at night. Dams on the Drin block its return, so Ohrid eels are stocked.

nodes.name: Dalmatian pelican
nodes.desc: A big fish-eater among the waterbirds that winter in the Ohrid reed beds. Wetland drainage caused its decline.

nodes.name: Marsh frog
nodes.desc: Large water frog of lakes and rivers. Mostly eats invertebrates but also takes small fish and other amphibians.

nodes.name: Dice snake
nodes.desc: Water snake of lake shores, recorded very often near Ohrid. It often eats fish and sometimes frogs and toads.

nodes.name: Beech marten
nodes.desc: Omnivore. GloBI records link it to rodents, frogs, snakes and grapes.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Generalist that eats rodents, frogs, snakes and fruit, per GloBI records.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Top predator of the surrounding mountains, with GloBI records of it eating rodents, foxes, martens and snakes.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore of the mountains. GloBI records show it eating rodents, foxes, grapes and maize.
